questions.prompt: In which months does Rwanda's **long rainy season** (Itumba) usually happen?
questions.explanation: Itumba, the long rainy season, runs from March to May. Mid-September to mid-December is the short rainy season (Umuhindo); June to August is part of the long dry season (Icyi); December to February is mostly the short dry season (Urugaryi).

questions.prompt: Which of these are **elements of weather**? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Temperature, rainfall, humidity and wind speed describe the state of the atmosphere, so they are elements of weather. Altitude is a **factor** that affects climate, and soil type is a property of the land, not of the air.

questions.prompt: Weather is the average condition of the atmosphere of a place, measured over about 30 years.
questions.explanation: That is the definition of **climate**. Weather is the condition of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, and it can change within hours.

questions.prompt: A town 1,400 m above sea level has a temperature of 25 °C. Temperature falls by about 6.5 °C for every 1,000 m of height. Estimate the temperature, in °C, at the top of a hill 2,600 m above sea level.
questions.explanation: Height difference $= 2600 - 1400 = 1200$ m, which is $1.2 \times 1000$ m. Temperature drop $= 1.2 \times 6.5 = 7.8$ °C. Temperature at the top $\approx 25 - 7.8 = 17.2$ °C.

questions.prompt: Which instrument shows the direction that the wind is blowing from?
questions.explanation: A **wind vane** (weather vane) points to the direction the wind comes from. Wind **speed** is measured with an anemometer.

questions.prompt: Name Rwanda's two rainy seasons and two dry seasons, giving the usual months of each. Then explain one way these seasons affect farmers.
questions.marking_guide: 1 mark: long rainy season (Itumba), March to May. 1 mark: short rainy season (Umuhindo), about mid-September to mid-December. 1 mark: both dry seasons with months: short dry season (Urugaryi), about mid-December to February, and long dry season (Icyi), June to about mid-September. 1 mark: one correct effect on farmers, e.g. crops are planted at the start of each rainy season (Season A from September, Season B from March); crops such as beans and maize are harvested and dried in the dry seasons; or crops may need irrigation or water storage in the long dry season. Accept English or Kinyarwanda names and months that are about right (within half a month).
questions.explanation: Rwanda has a long rainy season (Itumba, March–May), a long dry season (Icyi, June–mid-September), a short rainy season (Umuhindo, mid-September–mid-December) and a short dry season (Urugaryi, mid-December–February). Farmers plant at the start of the rains and harvest and dry crops in the dry seasons.
